cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The handbook gives fifteen miles per blank speed in a school zone.”?
cards.back: The handbook gives fifteen miles per hour as the maximum vehicle speed in a school zone.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “For a school bus carrying children on its blank specifies a maximum of forty-five miles per hour.”?
cards.back: For a school bus carrying children on its normal school route, the handbook specifies a maximum of forty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A school bus traveling on an interstate blank sixty-five miles per hour in the handbook.”?
cards.back: A school bus traveling on an interstate has a maximum speed of sixty-five miles per hour in the handbook.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “For passenger automobiles, including unloaded half-ton trucks, the blank range from forty to seventy miles per hour.”?
cards.back: For passenger automobiles, including unloaded half-ton trucks, the handbook lists an interstate speed range from forty to seventy miles per hour.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “For passenger automobiles on state or United States four-lane blank forty and maximum is sixty-five miles per hour.”?
cards.back: For passenger automobiles on state or United States four-lane highways, the listed minimum is forty and maximum is sixty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The usual maximum passenger-car speed on blank highways is fifty-five miles per hour.”?
cards.back: The usual maximum passenger-car speed on state and United States two-lane highways is fifty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The handbook lists fifty miles blank on the Natchez Trace Parkway.”?
cards.back: The handbook lists fifty miles per hour as the maximum on the Natchez Trace Parkway.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Treat the handbook’s usual speed limits as blank check both signs and the speedometer.”?
cards.back: Treat the handbook’s usual speed limits as subject to posted changes and check both signs and the speedometer.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Slow down for curves, blank and congested traffic.”?
cards.back: Slow down for curves, intersections, narrow or winding roads and congested traffic.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Poor weather or limited blank than ideal conditions.”?
cards.back: Poor weather or limited visibility requires a lower speed than ideal conditions.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A posted speed limit assumes ideal driving blank the speed is safe in every situation.”?
cards.back: A posted speed limit assumes ideal driving conditions rather than guaranteeing that the speed is safe in every situation.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Greater speed increases crash blank a fatal crash.”?
cards.back: Greater speed increases crash risk, including the risk of a fatal crash.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Signal before turning, changing lanes, blank out of a parallel-parking space.”?
cards.back: Signal before turning, changing lanes, passing or moving into or out of a parallel-parking space.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Use the vehicle’s turn blank turn or passing maneuver.”?
cards.back: Use the vehicle’s turn signals well before the intended turn or passing maneuver.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Do not repeat the turn signal of blank also plan to make that turn.”?
cards.back: Do not repeat the turn signal of the vehicle ahead unless you also plan to make that turn.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Do not use your left blinker to tell blank that driver must judge whether passing is safe.”?
cards.back: Do not use your left blinker to tell a following driver to pass; that driver must judge whether passing is safe.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Arm signals may be used by cyclists, drivers blank of certain older vehicles or farm equipment.”?
cards.back: Arm signals may be used by cyclists, drivers with failed blinkers and operators of certain older vehicles or farm equipment.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “When using an arm signal, fully extend the arm and maintain blank one hundred feet before slowing, stopping, turning or changing lanes.”?
cards.back: When using an arm signal, fully extend the arm and maintain the signal for at least one hundred feet before slowing, stopping, turning or changing lanes.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A straight outward arm and hand indicate blank lane change or departure from parallel parking.”?
cards.back: A straight outward arm and hand indicate a left turn, a right-to-left lane change or departure from parallel parking.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “An arm bent at the elbow with the hand blank a left-to-right lane change or entry into parallel parking.”?
cards.back: An arm bent at the elbow with the hand raised indicates a right turn, a left-to-right lane change or entry into parallel parking.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “An arm and hand pointing blank backward signal slowing or stopping.”?
cards.back: An arm and hand pointing down with the palm facing backward signal slowing or stopping.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Following too blank hazard.”?
cards.back: Following too closely creates a rear-end collision hazard.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “The handbook’s following-distance guidance calls for at least blank for each ten miles per hour of speed.”?
cards.back: The handbook’s following-distance guidance calls for at least one vehicle length of space for each ten miles per hour of speed.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Leave enough space ahead to allow blank lead vehicle changes speed suddenly.”?
cards.back: Leave enough space ahead to allow slowing or stopping if the lead vehicle changes speed suddenly.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “A following gap should blank the vehicle ahead.”?
cards.back: A following gap should also let you see around the vehicle ahead.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Leave additional following blank or bus.”?
cards.back: Leave additional following room behind a large truck or bus.

cards.back: The handbook’s stopping-distance chart assumes dry pavement, serviceable brakes and good tires.

cards.back: Slippery roads, poor weather, tiredness or intoxication can greatly change stopping distance from the chart’s ideal figures.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Thinking and reaction blank applies the brakes.”?
cards.back: Thinking and reaction distance occur before the driver applies the brakes.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Braking distance is the blank the vehicle stops.”?
cards.back: Braking distance is the travel from brake application until the vehicle stops.

cards.front: What words complete the handbook rule: “Total stopping distance includes both blank the distance traveled while braking.”?
cards.back: Total stopping distance includes both the pre-braking reaction travel and the distance traveled while braking.
